The maximum absolute daily move divided by mean absolute movement is a dimensionless jump-dominance score; dividing signed 20-day return by 1 plus this score suppresses jump-led paths while preserving gradual trend direction. Signed ten-day close return divided by the sum of ten dimensionless high-low ranges measures net directional displacement per unit of traversed intraday range. It preserves direction for expected continuation and shrinks two-sided noisy paths; the 1bp denominator floor is dimensionally consistent. Momentum/range neutralization and ordinary-efficiency comparison specifically test whether it adds more than low range or trend.

Negative five-day return is multiplied by ten-day mean dimensionless range divided by ten-day close-return volatility. Wide intraday ranges relative to close variation therefore amplify the opposite of recent direction, implementing disagreement-conditioned reversal; numerator and denominator share percentage scale and the 10bp floor bounds stale closes. Component and extreme-bar falsifications directly challenge generic reversal and volatility explanations.

Negative five-day return is scaled by maximum-daily-move share of total path movement and divided by five-day amount relative to a 60-day own-history baseline. Jump-dominated, low-participation shocks thus receive the strongest opposite-direction score, while gradual/high-participation moves are suppressed. The proposed plain-reversal, largest-day, and liquidity-decile tests are direct and the floors bound zero movement/amount.

The repaired raw score multiplies the exact negative half-wave of r10 by the exact positive half-wave of three-day mean close-versus-VWAP location. Four-quadrant synthetic evaluation leaves only prior decline plus positive stabilization active: gains, negative stabilization, and zero stabilization all yield zero before outer ordinal ranking. expected_direction=+1 therefore represents filtered rebound rather than generic reversal, and falsification covers all quadrants, each leg, and same-day execution feasibility.

Negative three-day VWAP return is scaled by three-day mean dimensionless range and inversely by own-history-normalized amount, so wide-range weak-participation displacement receives the largest opposite-direction score. All scales are trailing and dimensionless with a 0.1 participation floor; close-versus-VWAP, component-leg, limit-bar, and thin-decile tests can distinguish temporary impact from generic reversal.

Algebraic half-waves max(-r,0) and max(r,0) are squared and summed over 20 trailing days, yielding downside semivariance divided by upside semivariance. Larger factor values mean downside-dominant fragility and expected_direction=-1 correctly maps them to lower returns; the falsification covers outlier control, total volatility/tail-risk duplication, neutralization, and adjacent windows.

The AST averages open-to-low and open-to-high excursions as fractions of open over 20 days and forms their downside/upside ratio. Higher values unambiguously represent persistent intraday downside asymmetry, so expected_direction=-1 and selling-pressure/fragility tags align. The floor handles absent upside range, while outlier, volatility, limit-bar, and top-range exclusions directly test the stated failure modes.

The expression subtracts lag-one autocorrelation of upside half-wave magnitudes from that of downside half-wave magnitudes over the same 20-day trailing window. Larger scores therefore mean more persistent downside clustering and expected_direction=-1 maps them to underperformance. Sparse conditional samples are a real risk but are explicitly addressed by coverage, outlier, autocorrelation, semivariance, and volatility falsification requirements.

The five-day mean downside/upside half-wave ratio is divided by the corresponding 40-day ratio, so a value above one denotes recent acceleration into downside dominance relative to baseline. expected_direction=-1, state-transition tags, and 5/40 parameter rationale all match; smooth percentage-scale floors bound empty directional samples, and the falsification explicitly requires coverage plus level and fold-stability controls.
